purpose: Evidence that artifact identity (runId / report SHA-256) depends on the JavaScript engine version, from identical protocol, data and code identities.
note: Timestamps are deliberately omitted: this package must be byte-reproducible. Ordering is established by git history.
affectedClaim: experiments/results/audit-manifest.json:53 — 'Run the analysis twice from identical protocol, event artifact, and code identities; the report SHA-256 must be identical.'

method.harness: Read-only harness mirroring scripts/run-observed-experiments.mjs:20-29 with no file writes.

divergentFields.note: a small number of entries differ in the 17th significant digit

scientificImpact: NONE observed. The lognormal baseline still out-scores the mixture; the mixtureVsWeibull interval still straddles zero. This is a reproducibility and evidence-chain-identity defect, not a scientific-invalidity finding.
prediction: V8 transcendental drift (Math.exp/log/pow/sin or the Lanczos logGamma) explains the divergence.
observed: REFUTED. A direct probe across V8 12.4 and 14.1 produced BIT-IDENTICAL results for Math.exp, Math.log, Math.pow, Math.sin and the full Lanczos logGamma across eight shape values.
openQuestion: The divergence originates somewhere in the bootstrap accumulation path and has NOT been localized. This is deferred to red test C1.
alternativeExplanation: Candidate mechanisms not yet excluded: JIT tier-up changing floating-point association or fusion in hot loops; differing inlining of Math.pow; differing array/sort behaviour affecting accumulation order.
uncertainty: Only two Node versions sampled. Whether the committed artifact is reproducible on any Node 23.x or 24.x is UNKNOWN.
